newsitem.title: indonesia: Protest staged against Timorese in Austria mission.
newsitem.headline: Protest staged against Timorese in Austria mission.

text.p: About 40 youths staged a counter-protest outside the Austrian embassy in Jakarta on Wednesday as 33 East Timorese inside the compound waited to leave, witnesses said.

They said the demonstration was watched by about 20 uniformed police who allowed the youths, apparently mostly East Timorese, to hang banners on the embassy fence despite protests by an embassy official.
Some protesters shouted "Expel them!" while others climbed the fence unhindered to hang the banners which read "We love integration" and "Don't interfere in our internal affairs".
Eleonora Windisch, first secretary at the Austrian embassy, said earlier the 33 youths still in the mission's backyard were not seeking asylum and had not proved troublesome.
"They are intending to leave, but it doesn't mean they will be able to as there are police outside," Windisch told Reuters.

The 33 youths said they staged the break-in on Tuesday afternoon to meet a special envoy on East Timor of the U.N. Secretary-General who is in Jakarta as a part of a familiarisation trip to Indonesia and East Timor.
Only hours after the break-in, three of the youths were taken to meet special envoy Jamsheed Marker at the United Nations offices in Jakarta.

"We have met him and we told him of our aspirations," said Mariano Sabino Lopez, a spokesman for the group. "We do not mean to create hostility against the Indonesian government but (want) a way to open more dialogue on East Timor."
Marker told reporters after a meeting with Indonesia's official National Commission on Human Rights that he would take into account the views expressed by the youths.
Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas, on a visit to the United Arab Emirates, on Tuesday criticised the youths' action.
"Why have they gone into the embassy? Because it draws the attention of journalists. They are entitled to go to the U.N. offices in Jakarta but not on their terms," Alatas said.

The youths scaled the mission fence around 1 p.m. (0600 GMT) unfurling banners, including one saying "Viva Timor Leste" (Long Live East Timor) and asked embassy officials to set up a meeting with Marker, who returned to Jakarta on Monday after a three-day visit to East Timor.
Since September 1995, 108 East Timorese have entered foreign embassies in Jakarta and asked for political asylum, always granted by Portugal, the former colonial ruler of East Timor.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 and annexed it the following year in a move not recognised by the United Nations.
